pages.title: Angular Console Architecture
pages.purpose: Structure of the Angular 22 console (web/console): standalone+signals+zoneless, two-layer tab shell, the Injectable service layer, pure-function modules, the dialog system, and the dedup conventions that keep components thin.
instructions: Document that config-ops.ts serializeConfig preserves the original file's indentation/line-endings so diffs stay minimal — a key invariant for structured edits.

Map the layers: root shell (app.ts, storage status dot + main tabs), backend-pane sub-tabs (概览/分组/连接/流向/日志/规则/配置), service layer (backends/clash/vault/router/config-draft/live-stat/confirm/toast/share-health, all providedIn root), pure-function modules (config-ops/connections-model/flow-model/node-form/share-link/line-diff/group-board-model/rule-model), and the dialog family (rule-set/group/node-create/regroup/ssh-cred/share-config + confirm-dialog/toast replacing native confirm/alert).

Note build/deploy facts: `npx ng build --base-href=/edit/`, hashed multi-file output, Monaco served offline from /static/monaco/vs, CONSOLE_VERSION/PAGE_ORIGINS constants in models.ts must match Go allowOrigins.
Record the dedup收敛点 conventions: shared helpers live in util.ts (fmtBytes/latClass/runPool), line-diff.ts, node-form.ts; new features should extend these rather than re-implementing per component.
Write in Chinese; no real IPs in examples.

pages.title: System Overview & Topology
pages.purpose: The whole system on one page: the three independently-releasable units (Go vault-edit, Angular console, public NAS homepage), the runtime topology (admin host :9099/:9098, NAS rule buckets, sing-box routers), the read vs write channels, and the repo-file ↔ runtime-location mapping.
instructions: Cover the two write channels and why they are separate: POST /publish (rule buckets, zero-downtime 60s pull, VAULT_KEY only) vs POST /router/apply (whole config.json via SSH, ~1–2s断流, VAULT_KEY or clash secret).

Embed a mermaid flowchart of the topology: browser → admin host (vault-edit :9099 console + :9098 read-only files) → NAS (rule-set buckets) → routers (remote rule-set 60s pull; browser直连 clash_api :9090). No semicolons/pipes/angle brackets in labels.
Include the repo↔runtime table from HANDOFF.md/docs: which repo path lands where (binary /usr/local/bin/vault-edit, Angular产物 pageDir, web/index.html → NAS) and which script ships it.
Note the boundary invariant: the public entry serves only the desensitized homepage + rule-set + zashboard; /edit/ must 404 publicly.
Write in Chinese; keep placeholder hostnames (console.lan 等), never real IPs/secrets.

pages.title: Go Service (vault-edit) Module Map
pages.purpose: Module map of the single-package Go service: the full HTTP route table with implementing file per endpoint, shared helpers in httpx.go, env-driven configuration, startup order, and the deliberate degradation philosophy (warn-not-exit except VAULT_KEY).
instructions: Document config.go as the single source of env vars and whitelists: LISTEN, SHARE_*/SMB_*/SFTP_*, VAULT_KEY, bucket regex ^(rs-[a-z0-9-]+|bard-domains)$, ruleKeys (domain/domain_suffix/domain_keyword/ip_cidr), allowOrigins.

Explain main() startup order and the failure philosophy: only missing VAULT_KEY is fatal; SQLite/share/file-port failures log a warning and the service runs degraded, exposed via /health and /share/health.
List httpx.go conventions every handler reuses (writeJSON/fail/preflight/safeJoin) and the convention that new endpoints are added to main.go's route table comment.

Reproduce the route table from main.go's header comment (endpoint → implementing file) as the authoritative map; note the separate read-only file server on :9098 (files_server.go) that mounts only /rule-set/* and /health.
Write in Chinese; reference code as service/xxx.go:line where helpful.

pages.title: Auth, Secrets & CORS Model
pages.purpose: The layered credential model (VAULT_KEY, per-backend clash secrets, router SSH credentials), the dual /router/* auth scheme validated against router /version, exact-origin CORS requirements, and the public/private boundary.
instructions: Document the three credential layers and where each lives: VAULT_KEY only in /etc/vault-edit.env (0600, never repo/binary); clash secrets in browser localStorage + router config; SSH credentials server-side in SQLite routers table, never echoed back to the UI.

Explain the /router/* auth rule ('能访问 clash_api 就是有密钥'): the server validates the presented key against the router's /version; VAULT_KEY also works; the frontend sends X-Vault-Key = that backend's clash key (router.service.ts).

Record the CORS contract: browsers直连 clash_api, so each router's access_control_allow_origin must list the exact page origins (models.ts PAGE_ORIGINS ↔ service allowOrigins ↔ router config); origins must be exact scheme://host:port, never CIDR; WebSocket auth uses ?token= query.
State the security invariants: no secrets in repo or wiki, public surface is read-only (/edit/ 404 publicly), rotation requires syncing env + router configs.
Write in Chinese.

pages.title: SQLite Persistence
pages.purpose: The service's SQLite backend (db.go): table schema (kv/routers/publish_log/apply_log), WAL/single-writer choices, the one-time migration from legacy share.json/routers.json, and what each table is consumed by.
instructions: Document each table's owner and consumer: kv holds shareConfig (sharecfg.go hot swap); routers holds SSH credentials (router_store.go); publish_log records every /publish (bucket, bytes, sha, actor); apply_log records every apply/restart (host, changed, sha, backup, ms).
Embed a small mermaid erDiagram of the four tables and their producing flows if it clarifies; follow the mermaid syntax safety rules.

Explain the operational choices: modernc.org/sqlite (no CGO, cross-compilable), DB_FILE default /etc/vault-edit/sbm.db 0600 WAL, MaxOpenConns(1) for single-writer, lazy sync.Once open, migration failure is warn-and-continue.
Include the audit-trail role: GET /db/info exposes table row counts + last 5 publishes, used by the console and check scripts; apply_log backs rollback forensics.
Write in Chinese.

pages.title: Rule-Set Bucket Model
pages.purpose: The domain model of rule buckets: naming whitelist, .json/.srs pairing, the four allowed rule keys, bucket ordering/shadow-bucket semantics on routers, the 60s remote-pull effect, and bucket lifecycle (create/rename/delete, local-only rule-sets).
instructions: Capture the ordering semantics from runbook §2: routers evaluate route.rules in order, buckets are OR-inside; 'shadow buckets' preserve position when merging — moving entries between buckets changes semantics and requires re-running equivalence verification (the historical pitfall).
Cover lifecycle endpoints in buckets.go/files.go: index/create/rename/DELETE and the frontend rule-editor file tree that drives them.

Describe the effect model: routers pull remote rule-set URLs every ~60s, content changes detected by hash, so publishes need no restart; local-only rule-sets (cn_ip/hk_ip etc.) live on routers, not NAS.

Explain the invariants enforced in code: bucket names must match ^(rs-[a-z0-9-]+|bard-domains)$; publish accepts only the four ruleKeys with non-empty string arrays; .json and .srs are written as a pair and rename/delete moves both.
Write in Chinese.

pages.title: Rule Storage (ShareFS)
pages.purpose: The ShareFS storage abstraction (share.go): smb/sftp/local implementations, atomic tmp+rename writes, session reuse and retry, hot-swappable runtime config (sharecfg), and the separate read-only file port.
instructions: Cover the hot-config path: config persisted in SQLite kv, surfaced as GET/POST /share/config, POST /share/probe (test-without-save), POST /share/import (copy current share into local dir), applied live via applyShareConfig without restart.

Document the ShareFS interface contract (ReadFile with FileInfo for Last-Modified, WriteFile must be atomic via temp-name+rename so routers never pull half-written files, List, Describe) and the three implementations chosen by SHARE_MODE (smb default pure-Go SMB2 :445, sftp, local dir).
Explain session resilience: SMB session kept in-process, dropped and rebuilt once on failure (NAS reboot/network blip self-heal); publishes return 503 when the share is unavailable.
Explain the port split: :9099 console+API stays internal; :9098 (files_server.go) serves only /rule-set/* + /health so 'files对外、控制台对内' can be reverse-proxied independently.
Write in Chinese.

pages.title: Deployment & Release Units
pages.purpose: How code reaches the three runtime locations: deploy_service.sh (Go binary + systemd + env), deploy_console.sh (Angular build + Monaco, no service restart), deploy_web.sh (public homepage to NAS), the docker-compose alternative, and router onboarding.
instructions: Cover router onboarding: scripts/install_openwrt_singbox.sh pushes sing-box + init script + config with matching paths (/opt/sing-box, /etc/init.d/sing-box, /etc/sing-box/config.json) so /router/* can manage it; new routers join by pointing remote rule-set URLs at the same buckets and adding the exact page origins to access_control_allow_origin.

Document the Docker path: compose builds sbm/vault-edit with sing-box + Monaco inside, env_file .env (VAULT_KEY required, SHARE_MODE selection), ports 9099/9098, vault-data volume for SQLite — an alternative to bare-metal deploy, docs/deploy.md §11.
Present the three independently-releasable units with their scripts, targets, and post-conditions (the assertions each script makes: /health, /edit/ 200, entry js 200, /publish 401 without key).

Record operational gotchas that affect deploys: macOS needs LC_ALL=C LANG=C before deploy_console.sh (script aborts before upload otherwise); Monaco min/vs is laid once per VERSION; console deploys never restart the Go service; NAS nginx caches ~1min.
State the secrets rule for deployment: VAULT_KEY only via env (/etc/vault-edit.env 0600 or .env gitignored); nothing sensitive in repo or wiki.
Write in Chinese.

pages.title: Health Checks & Rollback
pages.purpose: The observability and recovery surface: /health and /share/health payloads, scripts/check.sh link-by-link assertions, router-side backup naming and rollback procedures, and the top recurring failure modes with their fixes.
instructions: Document /health's self-check payload (share mode/readiness, page/static dirs, files port, dbOK, routers file) and /share/health's two probes (file channel + public URL) — these are what check.sh and the console status dot trust.

List the top failure modes with causes/fixes from README+runbook: 401 (missing key), no ACAO (exact-origin CORS), /edit/ 白屏 (partial upload), Monaco missing (STATIC_DIR), rules not taking effect (hash-unchanged / 60s window / NAS write failure), EasyTier socat udp→tcp4 poisoning.

Record the backup/rollback conventions: router configs backed up as config.json.bak-<ts>-before-apply (apply flow does this automatically); console产物 edit.bak-<ts> on the admin host (timestamp is admin-host timezone); rule rollbacks = re-publish old content or restore NAS files.

Summarize check.sh's four sections: console dual entries + auth, public boundary (public /edit/ must 404, homepage/buckets 200), both routers' clash_api + the three exact CORS origins, and the bucket channel via /share/health.
Write in Chinese; use placeholder hostnames only.

pages.title: Testing & Verification
pages.purpose: How changes are verified before deploy: Go unit/regression tests, the console ops regression runner over bundled pure functions, real-router fixtures policy, the mock clash_api server, and the pre-deploy checklist.
instructions: Cover mock_clash.mjs acceptance mode: fake clash_api with ~420 connections serving the ng build at 127.0.0.1:8080, letting the full console run without routers (backend address = http://127.0.0.1:8080).

Document the console ops runner: npm run test:ops bundles config-ops.ts + shared-pool.service.ts to ESM via esbuild then asserts test/ops/*.mjs (fingerprint, pool-*, group-apply, cond-merge, string-rule-set); fixture-dependent cases skip without test/ops/fixtures/router-*.json, and fixtures contain real node secrets so they must never be committed.

Enumerate the Go suites and what each guards: service_test (pure functions), rules_summary_test (route rule summarization), equivalence_test (client-roster merge, public-rules rewrite, password-reuse口径, remote-script markers); run with cd service && go test ./..., plus gofmt -l and go vet as deploy gates.

Include the pre-deploy verification口径 from docs/architecture.md §5: ng build无ERROR, browser闭环 门禁→读取→表单→暂存→校验→应用→还原, post-apply re-check (/version 200, api port, egress 204), and the rule-semantics rule: any bucket restructuring requires the domain+IP dual-dimension equivalence check (IP-only rules give a false pass under domain-only testing).
Write in Chinese.

pages.title: Console Data Flow
pages.purpose: How the Angular console gets and moves data: backend registry in localStorage, browser-direct clash_api (REST + WS), live-stat single-poller fan-out, connection snapshot diffing, overview chart windows, the flow view's five-source merge, and mode/node writes.
instructions: Cover backend registry semantics in backends.service.ts: localStorage persistence, in-memory drafts (✎, lost on refresh), global vs per-backend key fallback, auto-reload on key/api change.

Document the data sources and cadences: clash_api REST (/version /proxies /connections /rules /configs) and WebSocket (/traffic /memory /connections /logs with ?token=), live-stat.service as the ONLY poller (subscribe/unsubscribe refcount, hidden-tab skip), overview windows (1/5/10 min, ws samples), flow view merging static config(30s)+connections(1.5s)+clients(30s)+delays(5s)+byte-activity.

Document write paths from the UI: selector switch PUT /proxies (Selector only; URLTest returns 400), PATCH /configs mode (the only writable runtime field), delay probes, connection kill single/filtered/all.
Embed a mermaid flowchart of the flow view's five data sources merging into the six-column band model if it clarifies; follow mermaid syntax safety rules. Write in Chinese.

Explain the connections diff model: ConnTracker.apply diffs adjacent snapshots into 活跃/已关闭(keep 500)/全部 tiers, computes rates from byte deltas and idle from last byte growth; search is per-word regex with literal fallback; grouping/sort/columns persist in localStorage.

pages.title: Publish Rule Bucket Flow
pages.purpose: End-to-end publish flow: console/CLI → POST /publish → auth → whitelist → structure validation → local sing-box rule-set compile → atomic write to ShareFS → publish_log → routers pick up within 60s; plus failure semantics at each stage.
instructions: Describe the frontend pre-validation in vault.service.ts (version/rules structure, key whitelist) and the verification loop afterwards (re-fetch confirm, zashboard rule=<bucket> hits, ≤60s wait, scripts/check.sh).

Document stage-by-stage failure semantics: 401 without X-Vault-Key; bucket whitelist rejection; parseRules errors are per-index; compile runs in a temp dir first so a failed compile never lands on NAS ('编译失败不落 NAS'); write is tmp+rename; publish_log row written on success.

Embed a mermaid sequenceDiagram: participants 编辑器 (rule-editor/publish.sh) → vault-edit /publish → ShareFS (NAS) → 路由 sing-box; show auth→validate→compile→write→log→60s pull. Keep labels free of semicolons/pipes/angle brackets.
Note the request-shape compatibility: content may be an object or a JSON-encoded string (CLI publish.sh sends the string form).
Write in Chinese.

pages.title: Router Config Apply Flow
pages.purpose: The router configuration write channel: draft staging in the console → /router/check → /router/apply SSH orchestration (backup→sing-box check→atomic replace→restart→health判定→failure rollback) with expectSha optimistic locking, plus restart-only, apistatus, clients and rules side endpoints.
instructions: Cover the companion endpoints: /router/restart, /router/check, /router/config (read + sha), /router/rules (structured summary), /router/clients (DHCP leases + ARP merge), /router/apistatus (gRPC via sing-box api CLI over SSH, degrade-to-empty), /public/rules preview/apply (rewrite route.rule_set[].url).

Describe the frontend staging chain: ConfigDraftService load→originalText/sha→dialog stage→save→serializeConfig preserving formatting→apply→reload; the config-pane gate (SSH creds → read → stage → validate → apply) and rollback convention (config.json.bak-<ts>-before-apply on the router).

Embed a mermaid sequenceDiagram of the apply orchestration: 浏览器 → /router/apply → router_ssh.go (SSH upload to /tmp, inline script) → 路由 (check → cp backup → mv replace → restart → pid+port health → rollback on failure). Include the 409-on-sha-mismatch optimistic lock.

Explain why orchestration lives server-side: sing-box has no reload/write-config API (Clash PUT /configs is a no-op; 1.15 services api is gRPC read-only), so config changes = file replace + restart; routers need no pre-installed scripts.

Record the hard-won pitfalls encoded in code: x/crypto/ssh stdout/stderr must not share one buffer; health = new pid AND :9090 listening (port alone is fooled by lingering sockets); 3-attempt backoff on dropbear handshake failures but no retry on Permission denied.
Write in Chinese.

pages.title: Storage Rewire & Public Rules Flow
pages.purpose: What happens when the NAS/rule entry point changes: probing and importing bucket files, hot-swapping ShareFS config, /share/health as the status-dot source, and rewriting route.rule_set[].url across routers via preview/apply.
instructions: Document /share/health's payload contract (file channel: mode/files/sample size/ms; public URL: status/bytes/ms) and that the console top-bar status dot and check.sh both consume it — new storage code must keep this accurate.

Explain public_rules.go: GET /public/rules/preview?base= computes per-router affected counts + old→new samples read-only; POST /public/rules/apply with confirm:true rewrites route.rule_set[].url through the same backup→check→replace→restart→rollback channel, skipping restart when changed=false.
Note the failure coupling: if the new share is unreachable, /publish returns 503 and /share/health goes red; rollback = re-point config back (kv) or restore prior entry.

Walk the rewire sequence: ⚙ dialog (share-config.ts) → POST /share/probe (test candidate without saving) → POST /share/config (persist to SQLite kv + applyShareConfig hot swap, including restarting the :9098 file port) → optional POST /share/import to copy existing buckets into local mode.
Write in Chinese.
